_format: skill-creator eval format. Run each prompt in a fresh session with and without the skill; grade the assertions. expect_trigger false marks a should-not-trigger probe.

evals.prompt: I'm uploading my product video to YouTube so I can share it with a few people for feedback. What do I fill in?
assertions: Recommends unlisted (link-only, comments allowed) over private for collecting feedback
Sets the audience to not made for kids and explains it would disable comments and end screens
Advises uploading the subtitle file
Raises the AI-voice licensing question if the voice is synthetic, including attribution on a free ElevenLabs plan
Gives a concrete title that leads with the outcome and ends with the product name

evals.prompt: tags? license? category? what else is under Show more when I upload this AI-voiced explainer for feedback?
assertions: Gives a concrete choice for tags, license, category, paid promotion, Shorts remixing and automatic chapters
Picks the Standard YouTube License over Creative Commons because free-plan synthetic audio is non-commercial
Says tags play a minimal role in discovery and keeps the list short
Says audio-only remixing cannot be blocked without Content Manager
Presents the fields in the order the upload dialog shows them

evals.prompt: Here's my title 'Get your coding agents off your laptop | Unfold' and my thumbnail says 'Ten agents. One laptop.' Good to go?
assertions: Points out that the thumbnail words repeat the title (agents, laptop) and proposes a title that adds to the thumbnail instead
Runs or recommends scripts/sheet.mjs to check the package
Keeps the product name last in any proposed title

evals.prompt: Make me a YouTube thumbnail for this explainer, I want to A/B test it.
assertions: Produces two to three variants that differ in promise or words, not only in colour
Keeps the words to about two to five and makes them add to the title instead of repeating it
Uses a frame from the video as background, cropped so the scene's own headline does not show behind the new words
Checks legibility at small size and keeps the bottom-right corner clear of important content
Explains Test & Compare judges by watch time share, runs up to about two weeks, and is unavailable for Shorts

evals.prompt: My video gets impressions but almost nobody clicks. What's wrong?
assertions: Compares click-through against the channel's own median rather than a universal benchmark
Looks at title and thumbnail as one promise and suggests testing meaningfully different variants
Checks the first 30 seconds of retention for a promise mismatch rather than only chasing clicks

evals.prompt: Write a LinkedIn post announcing our meetup next month.
assertions: Does not invoke youtube-upload-kit; LinkedIn post mechanics belong to another skill
